historical_reviews.deepseek: The policy/API versus physical AC split is correct, but the proposed filtered GET does not itself prove a write and the required CPU replacement is unreviewed.

original_test_intent: Prove that the verified SUT automatically powers on after a controlled AC restore when PowerRestorePolicy is AlwaysOn, and that the owner-approved Genoa CPU replacement subsequently powers on and boots without the documented early-DXE reboot failure.
original_method: Capture policy, hardware and workload baseline; set/read back AlwaysOn through the supported BMC interface; use the approved PDU to remove and restore AC and timestamp automatic power/boot; then safely isolate power, replace the exact approved CPU under ESD/thermal procedure, re-identify hardware and perform the defined post-swap power-on/POST/boot check; restore policy/hardware baseline when required.
manual_activity: A qualified operator controls workload shutdown, PDU/AC actions and CPU replacement, verifies physical identity/thermal installation and observes POST/boot while automation may perform protected policy read/write and collect power/health evidence.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC/System endpoint and PowerRestorePolicy property semantics
Original policy and approved final policy
Mapped PDU outlet, AC-off dwell, restore timing and independent console
Exact original/replacement CPU part numbers, socket, stepping and compatibility
Qualified hardware operator, ESD and thermal installation procedure
POST/boot deadline and early-DXE reboot-loop oracle
Pinned private script revision or reviewed equivalent
safety_requirements: Obtain explicit approval before policy write, shutdown, AC cycle and CPU swap
Never hot-pull a running service or unmapped power feed
Validate protected credentials and host identity; do not use curl -k/password command-line evidence
Confirm the SUT is de-energized before opening or replacing CPU
Use approved ESD, torque, socket-inspection and thermal-interface procedures
Stop on wrong outlet/CPU, BMC loss, unexpected power state, POST/thermal fault or reboot loop
Do not clear SEL, POST, dmesg or syslog evidence
Do not automatically retry a power or boot failure
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only target, policy, hardware and workload prechecks
Set/read back AlwaysOn only after explicit approval through the supported protected interface
Record PDU and chassis power-state timeline without replacing the physical operator
Capture pre/post CPU identity, POST, boot, thermal and event evidence
Track original/restored policy and hardware configuration
Report outcomes without assigning PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED
engineer_actions: Approve outage, PDU timing, policy mutation and final state
Approve exact CPU compatibility and physical service procedure
Operate or supervise AC and CPU swap
Define post-swap power-on/boot acceptance and recovery
Resolve failures and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A filtered Redfish GET can support policy discovery but does not prove the approved write, complete property readback, AC response or CPU-swap checkpoint; `-k` and password command lines are rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With approvals and recovery ready, set/read back AlwaysOn via the supported protected interface, execute one controlled PDU AC-loss/restore event and capture automatic power-on/boot, then perform the exact qualified CPU swap while de-energized and capture the defined post-swap power-on, POST and boot behavior.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Always on, AC off/on, CPU swap, Genoa 9654-to-9554 issue context and 10/20-minute estimates remain; the duplicated criterion is counted once, not dropped.

modernized_recommendation.status: APPROVAL-GATED ALWAYS-ON AC RESTORE AND CPU-SWAP BOOT QUALIFICATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use two linked evidence phases: policy/readback plus AC-restore automatic power timeline, then exact CPU before/after identity plus physical-service audit and POST/boot/reboot-loop observation, followed by baseline reconciliation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe outage/PDU control, CPU compatibility and physical-service gates, distinguishes the two acceptance checkpoints and secures the BMC interface.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Policy persistence alone does not prove AC-restore behavior; pre-swap automatic power-on does not prove post-swap boot stability or absence of the early-DXE loop.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Power loss and CPU replacement can cause data loss, socket/thermal damage, unsupported microcode behavior or boot loops; recovery may require restoring hardware or firmware outside the agent's control.

project_override_considerations: If the intended CPU pair differs from 9654-to-9554, the owner must publish the exact BOM and explain coverage of the referenced issue. The post-swap check must state whether power-on is manual or another AC-restore event; it cannot be inferred from the first checkpoint.
expected_evidence: Redacted SUT/BMC/PDU/CPU/BIOS/AGESA identity, baseline policy/hardware and approvals
Protected AlwaysOn write response and full readback
Controlled AC-off/on timestamps, chassis state and automatic power-on/boot evidence
CPU part/serial/stepping before and after plus ESD/socket/thermal service record
Post-swap power-on, POST, boot, thermal and early-DXE reboot-loop evidence
SEL/audit/console/OS events, recovery and final policy/hardware baseline plus engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria agree on AlwaysOn AC-restore behavior and successful post-CPU-swap power-on. The duplicate CPU criterion is redundant, while the exact post-swap stimulus needs owner definition but does not contradict the target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The high-risk hybrid test is executable once the owner supplies normal required inputs: supported policy interface, controlled PDU, exact CPU compatibility, qualified operator, acceptance timing and recovery.

review_improvement: Restores the omitted CPU-swap and early-DXE coverage, separates it from the AC-restore checkpoint and wraps both in recoverable power, hardware and evidence controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: AlwaysOn behavior is a BMC/chassis state transition caused by AC restoration, whereas a CPU swap changes boot topology, microcode and thermal installation. Because either phase can succeed while the other fails, their identities, stimuli and oracles must remain separate even though they share one recovery and final-state plan.
